item.title: Innovating in the Age of Longevity: Products, Processes, and People
item.content:encoded:
Céline Abecassis-Moedas, Universidade Católica Portuguesa

Sihem BenMahmoud-Jouini, HEC Paris

Chaiwoo Lee, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

Anna Cui, University of Illinois Chicago

Population ageing represents a major demographic shift with significant economic implications. With one in three people in OECD countries projected to be aged 65 and above by 2060, and older adults controlling nearly US$19 trillion in consumer spending, the silver economy demands systematic innovation management scholarship to address product development, organizational capabilities, and workforce composition.

While research on ageing has emerged across various disciplines, innovation management has been slow to study how silver innovations are conceived, developed, tested, and scaled. This special issue seeks to consolidate fragmented knowledge and establish innovation management as a core lens for understanding longevity, moving beyond deficit narratives toward value creation.

The issue welcomes conceptual, qualitative, and empirical work examining innovation adoption, design, business models, ecosystems, and age-diverse organizations across products, services, technologies, and talent management in B2C and B2B contexts and across cultural settings.

Appel publié par Journal of Product Innovation Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Adoption and diffusion of innovations across later-life stages
  • Segmentation approaches: chronological age, subjective age, gerontographic segments
  • Marketing communication and launch strategies for older users
  • Participatory design and co-creation with users across life stages
  • Universal design versus senior-specific product offerings
  • AI-enabled personalization, care robots, health monitoring, and voice interfaces
  • Business models for affordable silver innovations
  • Pricing and value-capture logics for heterogeneous older consumers
  • Public-private ecosystems in silver innovation scaling
  • Age-diverse and intergenerational innovation teams
  • Older innovators and entrepreneurs
  • Societal outcomes of longevity innovation: wellbeing, inclusion, digital equality
  • Organizational conditions enabling incumbents' response to ageing
